title: Student identity is directly disclosed by submitted identifiers
description: The student, as source, sends student ID together with course and assignment submission data to the portal. This act directly reveals the student's identity to the receiving system and associates it with the submitted work.
assumptions: The student ID is unique and identifies or is readily attributable to a specific student.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types but not detailed node taxonomy.

title: Submission contents and metadata can link repeated actions to the same student
description: The flow carries a work file, student ID, course, and submission timestamp. Together these attributes enable linking multiple submissions or portal interactions to the same student across time and courses if observed in transit or via flow metadata.
assumptions: An observer of the flow or its metadata can access identifiers and timestamps, or equivalent session/network metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ in the formal LINDDUN Pro taxonomy; applicability of linkability is high.

title: Assignment data and identifiers are exposed in transit
description: The data flow contains potentially personal and academic information: student ID, course enrollment, submission time, and the assignment file itself. If the transmission is intercepted or insufficiently protected, these data disclose personal and educational information.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, misconfigured, or bypassed; otherwise likelihood would be lower.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on actual transport protections, which are not specified.

title: Observed submission metadata can reveal student activity patterns
description: Even without full content access, the timing of assignment submissions, course context, and communication endpoints may allow an observer to infer study habits, deadlines met or missed, and participation patterns of the student.
assumptions: An attacker or intermediary can observe traffic metadata or partial payload fields.
uncertainty_note: This is a metadata-based detectability/inference threat; exact node id is approximate.

title: Portal can link submissions across courses and time to build a student profile
description: On receipt, the Grades Portal Web App can correlate the student ID, course, timestamps, and uploaded work across multiple submissions. This enables longitudinal linking of the student's academic behavior and performance-related activity.
assumptions: The portal stores or otherwise retains submission records over time.
uncertainty_note: Linkability at the destination is strongly applicable; exact node id is approximate.

title: Portal learns detailed personal and academic information from the submission
description: By receiving the assignment file plus student ID, course, and timestamp, the portal obtains information that may reveal the student's identity, enrollment, academic work, and potentially sensitive content contained in the file.
assumptions: The uploaded file may contain personal data beyond the minimum needed for submission.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate due to missing detailed taxonomy in context.

title: Portal may process submission data beyond the student's expectations
description: If the portal uses the uploaded file and metadata for secondary purposes such as analytics, plagiarism profiling, retention beyond course needs, or sharing with other systems without clear notice, the student may be unaware of the extent of processing.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, transparency, or just-in-time notice may be insufficient or absent.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on actual notice and processing practices, which are not specified.

title: Collection of full assignment file and metadata may exceed necessity
description: The destination may collect or retain more personal data than necessary for the purpose of accepting an assignment, for example retaining detailed timestamps, embedded document metadata, or unnecessary identifiers when less data would suffice.
assumptions: The system may not minimize uploaded content, metadata extraction, or retention.
uncertainty_note: Necessity/compliance assessment depends on the portal's actual purpose specification and retention design.

title: Portal shares more personal data than strictly necessary with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. If all of these attributes are not strictly required for each request type, the source process causes avoidable disclosure of personal data across an internal boundary, contrary to data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes some routed operations may not require the full attribute set for processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement; retrieved context confirms Dd applicability and minimality principle but did not provide the exact Dd subtree citation.

title: Data flow contains direct identifier for the student
description: The transmitted payload includes student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone able to observe or access the flow can identify which student's submission or grading request is being handled.

title: Grading service processes identified student data
description: The assignment & grading service receives and processes requests containing student id together with course and file reference, meaning the destination processes identified data rather than anonymous or pseudonymous data.

title: Submission and grading requests can link student activity across courses or assignments
description: Because the flow combines student id, course, file reference, and requesting role in repeated requests, the data in transit can be used to correlate multiple actions to the same student and build a picture of their academic activity over time.
uncertainty_note: Linkability subtree citation is based on best judgement; retrieved context did not include the exact L subtree node.

title: Flow metadata and payload reveal academic activity to unintended observers
description: Even aside from content, the routing of submission and grading requests between portal and grading service reveals that a particular student is interacting with a specific course or assignment context. If the flow is observable by intermediaries or logs, this creates avoidable disclosure of educational activity data.
assumptions: Assumes network, middleware, or logging layers may expose payload fields or metadata beyond strictly authorized components.
uncertainty_note: Exact Dd subtree citation is approximate; applicability depends on observability of the flow and surrounding infrastructure.

title: Excessive disclosure from grading service to storage
description: The grading service stores a submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for the storage purpose, P2 discloses more personal data to the store than needed, violating data minimisation.
assumptions: Assumes some stored attributes may be optional for the immediate storage purpose, or could be reduced/pseudonymised.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN data-disclosure/minimisation concepts; exact subnode may differ in the canonical tree.

title: Linkability via combined assignment metadata in transit
description: The flow carries a submitted file together with student id, course, and submission time. Even without inspecting file contents, this combination can link multiple submissions to the same student across courses or over time.
assumptions: Assumes the identifiers and metadata are visible to components or observers handling the flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node citation is approximate; applicability depends on whether the metadata is exposed on the flow beyond the intended endpoints.

title: Identifiability from student identifier and submission metadata in transit
description: Because the flow includes a direct student identifier plus course and timestamp metadata, the student is directly identifiable on this flow, and the metadata can further single out the individual submission.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is directly identifying within the system context and that the flow can be observed or processed by intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node citation is approximate; the threat clearly applies at least at the generic identifiability level.

title: Stored assignment records enable linkage across submissions
description: By receiving and storing assignment files together with student id, course, and submission time, the Assignment Store can correlate multiple records belonging to the same student across assignments and courses, enabling linkage beyond what may be necessary for grading.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 retains records in a form queryable by student id or equivalent key.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node citation is approximate; threat depends on retention and query capabilities of DS1.

title: Stored records make students identifiable
description: The Assignment Store receives direct identifiers and associated submission metadata, making the student identifiable within stored records and potentially to anyone with access to the store.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores the student id in clear or otherwise readily attributable form.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node citation is approximate; generic identifiability threat is clear.

title: Unnecessary disclosure through persistent storage of personal data
description: Persistently storing the assignment file together with student id, course, and exact submission time may disclose more personal data than necessary at the destination, especially if some fields could be omitted, coarsened, or separated.
assumptions: Assumes not all attributes are strictly required to be stored together for the full retention period.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN disclosure/minimisation concepts; exact subnode may differ.

title: Teacher submits identified account credentials and role context
description: When logging in and requesting the review queue, the teacher sends identified data to the portal, such as username/email, authentication material, and implicitly their teacher role or course affiliation. This directly identifies the individual to the system.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes account identifiers and/or credentials tied to a specific teacher account.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: The login and queue-request flow may expose stable identifiers or metadata in transit, such as account name, session identifiers, IP address, timing, and requested course context. Observers of the flow could use this to link multiple actions to the same teacher over time.
assumptions: Assumes network-visible metadata or stable protocol/application identifiers are present on the flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability was not provided in the retrieved context; tree_node is best-effort.

title: Teacher identity may be exposed in transit
description: The data flow can contain directly identifying information about the teacher, including login identifier and possibly course-specific request parameters that identify the teacher to anyone able to inspect the transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the flow is observable by an attacker or intermediary and contains direct identifiers at the application or protocol layer.

title: Portal learns teacher review activity and course-assignment details
description: By receiving the login and queue request, the web app can determine that this teacher is active at a particular time and infer which courses or submission queues they are responsible for. This reveals behavioral and role-related information beyond mere authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the request specifies or implies course membership or review responsibilities.
uncertainty_note: Specific detectability subtree id was not available in the retrieved context; tree_node is best-effort.

title: Portal may process login/request data without sufficient transparency or consent basis
description: The destination process may collect and use teacher login and queue-request data, including activity logs and course-assignment context, in ways not clearly communicated to the teacher or not aligned with the expected purpose of accessing submissions.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notice, purpose limitation, or internal-use constraints may be insufficient for this processing.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on organizational policy and legal basis, which are not provided here; subtree id is best-effort.

title: Portal discloses more student data to the teacher than is strictly necessary
description: The web app intentionally shares student names, work content, and submission times with the teacher. If all of these fields are not necessary for the teacher's task in the specific context, the source process causes avoidable disclosure of personal data, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes some displayed attributes or full submission content may exceed what the teacher needs for the immediate educational purpose, or may be shown for students outside the teacher's responsibility.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as best-fit explicit disclosure/minimization node; exact sub-node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Submission metadata in transit can disclose sensitive student information
description: The flow includes submission times and likely identifiers tied to named students. Even aside from the work content itself, these metadata can reveal behavior patterns, participation, lateness, or special circumstances. If exposed in transit or through observable message characteristics, this creates avoidable disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the transmission or observable flow characteristics could be accessed by parties beyond the intended teacher, or that metadata are more detailed than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node for implicit/metadata disclosure is approximate.

title: Teacher can link multiple submissions and timestamps to build detailed student profiles
description: By receiving identified submissions over time, the teacher can correlate names, work content, and submission times across assignments. This enables linking records into a broader profile of each student's behavior and performance beyond a single submission event.
assumptions: Assumes repeated use of the portal and identifiable student records across multiple submissions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linking node selected; exact sub-node id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Displayed submissions directly identify students to the recipient
description: The flow contains student names alongside their work and timestamps, allowing the teacher to identify individual students. If identification is not necessary in some review contexts, or if pseudonymous review would suffice, this is an avoidable identifiability threat.
assumptions: Assumes there are contexts such as blind marking, moderation, or preliminary review where direct identification is not strictly required.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on whether identified review is necessary for the educational process.

title: Students may be unaware that teachers can view detailed submission metadata
description: If students are not clearly informed that teachers will see not only their submitted work but also exact submission times and associated identifiers, the receipt and use of this data by the teacher may be insufficiently transparent.
assumptions: Assumes notices or UI explanations do not clearly communicate what teachers can see.
uncertainty_note: Transparency/usawareness depends on the portal's notices and educational policy context.

title: Disclosure of submissions to the teacher may exceed the consent or legal expectation communicated to students
description: If students were not given a clear legal basis, policy notice, or meaningful choice regarding teacher access to names, content, and timestamps, the destination's receipt and use of the data may not align with consent or another properly communicated processing basis.
assumptions: Assumes consent or another lawful basis/notice is relevant and may be inadequately communicated or scoped.
uncertainty_note: In many school contexts processing relies on institutional necessity rather than consent, so applicability depends on governance and jurisdiction.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a grade/feedback entry
description: The flow carries a grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id from the teacher to the portal. If the submission is not strongly bound to the teacher's authenticated session and recorded with reliable audit evidence, the teacher may later repudiate having entered or changed the grade or feedback.
assumptions: Applies if submission events are not protected by strong authentication, integrity protection, and tamper-evident audit logging.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id is based on best judgement; exact subnode may differ in the project's LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Grade submission flow can expose identities of teacher and student in transit
description: The transmitted payload contains direct identifiers (student id, grader id) and sensitive educational content (grade and written feedback). If the flow is observable in transit, an attacker could identify the student and teacher associated with a specific assessment event.
assumptions: Applies if transport confidentiality is absent, weak, or bypassed, or if intermediary systems can inspect payload contents.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may be more specific than the generic identification node used here.

title: Assessment submissions can be linked across events via stable identifiers
description: Because the flow includes stable student and grader identifiers, observers of the flow or intermediaries handling it can correlate multiple submissions over time, linking a teacher's grading activity across students and a student's assessment history across assignments.
assumptions: Applies where stable identifiers are reused across transactions and visible to network observers, logs, or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; a more specific linkability subnode may exist.

title: Sensitive grade and feedback content may be disclosed in transit
description: The flow contains confidential educational records and potentially sensitive free-text feedback. If intercepted or exposed through transport-layer weaknesses, debugging proxies, or verbose network logging, unauthorized parties could learn the student's performance details and teacher comments.
assumptions: Applies if end-to-end transport protection, certificate validation, and logging minimization are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subnode may differ.

title: Portal may collect or retain more grading data than necessary
description: On receipt, the portal may store the full feedback text, identifiers, timestamps, client metadata, and revision history longer than needed for grading purposes. Excessive retention or collection at the destination increases privacy impact for both students and teachers.
assumptions: Applies if the portal stores ancillary metadata or retains records beyond defined educational and legal needs.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node selection; a more specific detectability/data minimization subnode may exist depending on the catalog used.

title: Teachers or students may be insufficiently informed about downstream use of submitted grades and feedback
description: After receiving the data, the portal may reuse grade and feedback information for analytics, performance monitoring, moderation, or sharing with other systems without clearly informing the teacher or affected student. This creates a lack of awareness about how the submitted assessment data is processed.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices, in-context explanations, or role-specific transparency about secondary uses are incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may be more specific.

title: Portal processing of grades and feedback may occur without a valid legal basis or beyond stated educational purposes
description: Grades, feedback text, and identifiers are personal data and may be subject to education-sector rules and data protection law. If the portal processes or repurposes this data beyond the necessary educational function, or without an appropriate legal basis and policy alignment, the flow contributes to non-compliance.
assumptions: Applies if governance, purpose limitation, retention rules, or access controls are not aligned with applicable law and institutional policy.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends heavily on jurisdiction and institutional context; node id is best judgement.

title: Excessive grade-record content disclosed to the database
description: The grading service writes a rich grade record containing student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. If all fields are not strictly necessary for the intended storage purpose, P2 discloses more personal data than needed to DS2, increasing privacy exposure for both students and graders.
assumptions: Assumes some fields (for example detailed feedback, grader id, or precise timestamp) may not be necessary for every storage/use case.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Grade records in transit enable linkage of student academic events
description: The flow carries stable identifiers and contextual attributes together: student id, course, grade, grader id, and timestamp. Observing or correlating this transmission can link multiple grading events to the same student, course enrollment, and grader over time.
assumptions: Assumes the flow or its metadata can be observed, logged, or correlated by intermediaries or monitoring components.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; linkage clearly applies, but exact sub-node is not available in the provided context.

title: Identifiability of student and grader from transmitted record
description: Because the transmitted record includes student id and grader id, the data flow directly identifies natural persons. Even if payload protection is partial, associated metadata and contextual fields may still reveal who is being graded and who performed the grading.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are directly identifying within the system context.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact threat-tree sub-node not present in retrieved context.

title: Database retention and secondary use may disclose more grade data than necessary
description: Once DS2 receives the full grade record, storing it indefinitely or making it available for broader analytics, auditing, or administrative access can disclose personal data beyond the original grading purpose.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 may retain records for long periods or support secondary uses beyond immediate grade recording.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in destination-side processing/storage behavior; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Students or graders may be unaware of stored grading metadata
description: DS2 stores not only the grade outcome but also feedback, grader id, and timestamp. Data subjects may not be sufficiently aware that these metadata are recorded and retained in the grade records database, limiting transparency about processing.
assumptions: Assumes notices or interfaces do not clearly explain all stored fields and retention/usage.
uncertainty_note: Awareness threat is plausible for this destination, but depends on the surrounding notice and UX design.

title: Storage of grade records may exceed consent or legal expectation
description: If DS2 stores detailed feedback, grader identifiers, or timestamps without an appropriate legal basis, policy justification, or alignment with user expectations, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent, contract, legitimate-interest balancing, educational-law basis, or policy constraints may not fully cover all stored attributes.
uncertainty_note: This is a compliance-oriented threat and depends on the actual legal basis and institutional policy, which were not provided.

title: Student request contains identified data
description: To request grades and feedback, the student typically sends identifiers such as login session data, student number, or account identity to the web app. This means identified data is disclosed by the source as part of the request.
assumptions: Assumes the grades portal requires the student to be authenticated or otherwise identified to retrieve their own records.

title: Identity may be exposed in transit metadata
description: The request flow can carry identifiers directly in message contents, headers, cookies, tokens, or observable metadata that tie the request to a specific student, enabling identification on the flow.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers or session-related metadata traverse this flow.
uncertainty_note: Exact transport protections and protocol details are not provided.

title: Web app processes identified student request
description: The grades portal web app receives and processes the student's request together with identity information to locate and return the correct grades and feedback, constituting processing of identified data at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes the app uses the student's identity or account context to resolve the requested grades.

title: Grade-request traffic can link repeated actions to the same student
description: Repeated requests on this flow may be linkable through stable identifiers such as account IDs, session cookies, IP address patterns, or device/browser fingerprints, allowing correlation of multiple grade-access events to the same student.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or metadata are observable across requests.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node chosen by best judgement; exact node id may vary with the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Request reveals student interest in specific academic results
description: By receiving the request, the web app learns that this identified student is accessing grades and feedback at a particular time, which discloses behavior and potentially sensitive academic concerns or events.
assumptions: Assumes access events are logged or otherwise observable by the destination.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node chosen by best judgement; exact node id may vary with the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Student request may be logged as evidence of access
description: The destination may create logs, audit trails, or transaction records showing that the student requested grades and feedback. Such records can later be used to prove the student's action, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes the portal maintains access or audit logs for security or compliance purposes.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node chosen by best judgement; exact node id may vary with the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Portal may disclose grades or feedback to the wrong student account/session
description: When the web app sends grades and teacher feedback, an authorization or session-binding error could cause one student's records to be shown to another student. This would identify the data subject and reveal personal academic information to an unintended recipient.
assumptions: Assumes the portal relies on account/session context to determine which student's records to display.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context only provided applicable threat types/positions, not detailed node mappings.

title: Grades and feedback could be intercepted in transit
description: The flow carries personal academic information from the portal to the student. If transport protection is absent, weak, or downgraded, an eavesdropper on the network path could learn the student's grades and teacher feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the communication traverses a network where interception is possible if not properly protected.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly if TLS or equivalent transport protection is missing or misconfigured.

title: Traffic metadata may link a student to specific academic results access
description: Even if content is encrypted, observing that a particular student account/device is accessing the grades portal at specific times may allow an observer to link that student to grade-checking events or academic-status-related interactions.
assumptions: Assumes a network or service observer can see communication metadata such as endpoints, timing, or frequency.
uncertainty_note: This is a metadata-based linkability threat at the flow level; exact node id is best-judgement.

title: Displayed grades may be exposed on the student's device or surroundings
description: Once received, the grades and feedback are rendered on the student's device. Shoulder surfing, shared devices, browser caching, notifications, or screen capture on the recipient side could disclose the information to others nearby or using the same device.
assumptions: Assumes the student may use a shared or observable device/environment.
uncertainty_note: Included because disclosure can arise at the destination upon receipt/display, though some models may treat endpoint exposure outside strict system scope.

title: Portal may provide grades/feedback without adequate notice about processing and display
description: If the portal displays grades and teacher feedback without clearly informing the student how this information is sourced, updated, retained, or who can access it, the flow may lack sufficient transparency and awareness for the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes transparency obligations apply to this educational context and are not already met elsewhere in the service.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends strongly on applicable policy/regulatory requirements and what notices are provided outside this specific flow.

title: Parent submits identified account credentials and child-linked request
description: The parent initiates login and a grades request using an account that is explicitly linked to a specific child. This causes identified data about the parent-child relationship to be shared with the portal, enabling direct identification of both the parent account and the associated student.
assumptions: The login/request includes account identifiers or credentials that uniquely identify the parent account and its linkage to a child account.

title: Parent-child relationship may be linkable from request metadata in transit
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata on the flow such as account identifiers, session identifiers, request paths, or repeated access patterns for a specific child record can enable linking multiple requests to the same parent and child, revealing the persistent parent-child association.
assumptions: Observable metadata or stable identifiers are present on the flow and can be correlated across requests.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a more specific linkability node.

title: Portal learns the parent's interest in the child's grades
description: By receiving the login and grades request, the portal can detect that this specific parent is requesting this specific child's grades at a particular time. This reveals behavioral information about the parent's actions and the parent-child association beyond merely storing an account identifier.
assumptions: The portal logs or otherwise processes the request in a way that exposes the parent's access behavior.
uncertainty_note: Specific detectability subtree citation is approximate because no detectability nodes were provided in the retrieved context.

title: Portal may process parent-child linkage and grade-access request without sufficient consent transparency
description: The destination process receives and processes data about a parent account linked to a child account and the parent's request for grades. If the portal does not provide clear notice, appropriate authorization basis, or consent/permission handling for this family linkage and access, the processing may be non-compliant with applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable policy or legal requirements require transparency, authorization, or consent management for parent access to a child's educational records.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction, school policy, and whether another lawful basis besides consent applies; subtree citation is best judgement.

title: Portal discloses excessive educational detail to the parent
description: The web app shares the child's grades, teacher feedback, and submission history with the parent. If the portal exposes more detail than necessary for the parent's legitimate purpose, or shows records for the wrong child or class context, the child becomes identifiable through rich educational records and sensitive performance information is revealed.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may present detailed per-assignment history and narrative feedback, and that access-control or data-minimisation weaknesses are plausible for this view.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Transmission metadata can link parent and child
description: Even if the content is protected, the flow itself can reveal that a specific parent account is accessing a specific child's grades portal at particular times. Network or application metadata may therefore enable linkage between the parent and the child's educational record.
assumptions: Assumes observable metadata such as session identifiers, URLs, timing, or account references exist on the communication path.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly where transport/application metadata is observable by intermediaries or logs.

title: Educational records may be exposed in transit
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history are personal data. If the flow is not adequately protected in transit, an eavesdropper could learn the child's academic performance and related information.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transport protection, weak session handling, or leakage through browser caches, referrers, or mixed-content requests.
uncertainty_note: General disclosure-in-transit threat; exact attack surface depends on implementation.

title: Parent may further disclose the child's academic information
description: Once received, the parent can store, screenshot, print, or share the child's grades and feedback beyond the original educational context, causing onward disclosure of the child's personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the parent device or user behavior is in scope for destination-side privacy effects in LINDDUN Pro.
uncertainty_note: Destination-side disclosure by an external entity is a plausible privacy outcome, though some teams may treat this as partly outside direct system control.

title: Parent may not understand how much student data is being revealed
description: The recipient may be shown detailed grades, feedback, and submission history without clear notice about scope, retention, or why each category is available. This can undermine transparency and informed understanding of the child's data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the portal lacks clear contextual notice or explanation for the displayed data categories.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on applicable transparency obligations and portal notice design.

title: Administrator can deny having created, modified, or disabled accounts or parent-child links
description: If the administrator's actions on this flow are not strongly bound to their identity and time, the administrator may later repudiate having submitted specific account-management changes, including role assignments and parent-child relationship changes.
assumptions: Applies if requests are not protected by strong authentication, signed requests, or tamper-evident audit logging at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed Nr subtree nodes.

title: Account-management payload in transit can identify students, parents, and administrators
description: The flow carries names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. If intercepted or insufficiently protected in transit, these attributes can directly identify involved individuals and reveal who is linked to whom.
assumptions: Applies if transport confidentiality/integrity protections are absent, weak, or bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detailed I subtree mapping was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Relationship and role metadata in transit enable linkability
description: Even aside from direct identifiers, the combination of account role changes and parent-child link updates can be used to correlate records across sessions or systems, linking a parent to a specific child and linking administrative actions to particular families.
assumptions: Especially relevant if the same identifiers, emails, or stable relationship references recur across transactions or are observable by intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detailed L subtree mapping was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Grades Portal can learn sensitive role and family-relationship information beyond what is necessary
description: On receipt, the web app processes names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships. If it collects, stores, or exposes more of this account-management data than needed for the specific administrative task, it creates a detectability/disclosure risk by making sensitive family associations and role assignments observable within the system.
assumptions: Applies if the destination stores full payloads, exposes them in admin screens/logs, or makes them queryable beyond operational necessity.
uncertainty_note: Classification between Detectability and broader disclosure is somewhat judgment-based here because only the top-level mapping context was provided.

title: Portal processing may fail to keep administrators and families unaware of relationship-data handling
description: If the portal does not clearly communicate how names, emails, roles, and parent-child links are stored, propagated, and used after receipt, affected parties may be unaware of the extent of processing of family relationship data.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices, in-product explanations, or admin guidance do not adequately cover this processing.

title: Portal may process account and relationship data in ways users did not expect
description: Using submitted names, emails, roles, or parent-child links for secondary purposes—such as analytics, profiling, or broader internal sharing—would exceed the expectations tied to straightforward account administration.
assumptions: Applies if the destination reuses the data beyond account lifecycle management and access control.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detailed U subtree mapping was not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Portal may process parent-child relationship data without an appropriate legal basis or policy alignment
description: Parent-child links and associated identity data may constitute personal data requiring a defined legal basis, purpose limitation, and governance. If the portal receives and processes these data without appropriate authorization, policy alignment, or regulatory compliance, non-compliance risk arises.
assumptions: Applies if there is no documented lawful basis, role-based authorization model, retention rule, or school policy covering this processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detailed Nc subtree mapping was not provided in the retrieved context.

description: P2 writes account records plus parent-child relationship links into DS3. These are personal data and relationship data; if the directory does not strictly need all attributes or all relationship links for its purpose, the write causes avoidable disclosure by design, violating data minimisation.
assumptions: DS3 is used as an account directory and may not require the full set of grading-service-held attributes or all parent-child linkage details.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimisation structure; exact subnode may differ in your local catalog.

title: Account directory can link student and parent identities across contexts
description: By receiving and storing parent-child relationship links together with account records, DS3 can correlate student accounts with parent accounts and potentially with other directory-held identifiers. This enables linkability between data subjects and across roles or contexts beyond what each individual record would reveal alone.
assumptions: DS3 stores multiple identifiers or records that can be queried or combined, and the parent-child links persist beyond a transient operational need.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; the threat itself is grounded in explicit storage of relationship links enabling correlation.

title: Relationship links in the directory can identify individuals and households
description: Parent-child relationship links, especially when combined with account records, can directly identify a child, a parent, or a family unit even if some fields are otherwise limited. Receipt and storage of these links in DS3 therefore increases identifiability of the involved data subjects.
assumptions: Account records contain identifiers or quasi-identifiers such as names, usernames, emails, class membership, or contact details.
uncertainty_note: Subnode id is best-judgement; identifiability clearly applies even if your local tree labels differ.

title: Directory storage of family relationships may reveal sensitive role and household information
description: Storing parent-child links in DS3 exposes relationship and household structure information. Even if not special-category data by itself, such relationship data can reveal private aspects of family composition and associations that data subjects may not expect to be broadly visible within an account directory.
assumptions: DS3 is accessible to administrative functions or other services beyond the grading workflow, increasing the audience for inferred family information.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure/threat boundary between detectability and disclosure can vary by methodology wording; here the concern is that existence and structure of relationships become observable.

title: Repurposing directory data for non-grading uses may be unexpected to users
description: Users may reasonably expect grading operations to use account data for assessment administration, but not expect parent-child relationship links written by the grading service to be retained in a general account directory and reused by other services. This creates an unawareness risk about where relationship data is stored and for what purposes it is processed.
assumptions: Notices or UI do not clearly explain that grading-derived account and family-link data are stored in DS3 for broader directory use.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency around this write and subsequent uses is limited; if notices are explicit, this threat may be reduced.

title: Writing family-link data into the directory may exceed the stated purpose or legal basis
description: If DS3's defined purpose is account management, storing parent-child relationship links originating from grading operations may be incompatible with that purpose unless specifically justified and governed. This raises non-compliance risk with purpose limitation, data minimisation, and potentially lawful-basis requirements.
assumptions: The system's privacy notice, records of processing, or access-governance model do not explicitly cover this category of relationship data in the directory.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on actual governance and legal basis; threat is genuine where purpose compatibility has not been established.

title: Excessive disclosure of full academic records to third-party host
description: The nightly backup/replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party cloud hosting provider. This may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for hosting/backup purposes, violating data minimization if the provider does not need all fields in identifiable form.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a separate third party and not merely an internal processor with strictly equivalent controls; backups include identifiable student/staff records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected as best-fit for avoidable explicit disclosure/minimization; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Recipient-side overexposure and secondary access to backup contents
description: Once received by the cloud hosting provider, the replicated backup may be accessible to provider personnel, subprocessors, support channels, or management interfaces beyond what is necessary to deliver the service. This creates avoidable disclosure at the destination through storage, administration, or onward handling of the full dataset.
assumptions: Provider staff or subprocessors can potentially access stored backup data or metadata during operations, support, or incident handling.
uncertainty_note: Exact destination-side Dd sub-node is approximate; threat clearly concerns avoidable disclosure caused by recipient-side storage/processing.

title: Linkability via stable replicated identifiers across datasets
description: The transferred backup contains account-directory data together with grades and assignments. Stable identifiers such as usernames, student IDs, email addresses, or internal account keys can enable linking records across multiple backup snapshots and across other datasets available to the hosting provider, revealing longitudinal profiles of individuals.
assumptions: Backups preserve stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers and the provider can observe multiple snapshots or correlate with other tenant/provider-side data.
uncertainty_note: Sub-node is best-fit for linkability from shared identifiers in transit; exact numbering may differ across catalogs.

title: Identifiability of students and staff in backup payload
description: Because the flow ships full grade records, assignments, and directory information, individuals are likely directly identifiable from names, emails, usernames, student numbers, or combinations of attributes contained in the replicated dataset.
assumptions: The backup is not strongly pseudonymized before transfer and contains direct or readily re-identifiable attributes.
uncertainty_note: Exact I sub-node chosen as direct identifiability best-fit.

title: Detectability of academic activity through backup traffic patterns
description: Even if payload contents are protected, the existence, timing, size, and frequency of nightly replication can reveal that the service processes substantial volumes of academic records and when activity spikes occur, making the presence of particular cohorts, grading periods, or assignment cycles detectable.
assumptions: A network observer or the provider can observe traffic metadata such as timing and volume.
uncertainty_note: Threat is based on metadata detectability at the flow level rather than payload inspection.

title: Processing by cloud host may exceed users' consent or reasonable expectations
description: Students and staff may not reasonably expect their full grades, assignments, and directory data to be replicated to a third-party cloud host, especially if this transfer was not clearly communicated or covered by an appropriate legal basis. The destination's receipt and processing can therefore create non-compliance with consent/transparency requirements.
assumptions: Relevant notices, contracts, or legal bases may be incomplete, unclear, or narrower than this full-data replication.
uncertainty_note: Modeled under Nc because the privacy risk depends on legal basis/transparency rather than purely technical exposure; exact node numbering is approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure from grade records database
description: The grade records database may disclose more grade-related personal data than is necessary when serving P2's request to build student, parent, and teacher views. A broad read can expose full grade histories, comments, identifiers, or records for users beyond the specific audience/view being generated.
assumptions: DS2 can return broad record sets and field-level minimization is not enforced at the source.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement at a high level because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Linkability via grade-record identifiers and metadata in transit
description: Data on DF15 may contain stable student, parent, teacher, class, or assignment identifiers that allow records and requests to be linked across sessions or contexts. Even if content is expected, the combination of identifiers and request metadata can enable correlation of a learner's performance across multiple views.
assumptions: The flow carries persistent identifiers or metadata such as student IDs, class IDs, assignment IDs, or timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Applies if the flow exposes stable identifiers or correlatable metadata; exact fields are not specified.

title: Identifiability of students and related parties in transit
description: Grade records sent on DF15 may directly identify students, and may also identify parents and teachers through names, account identifiers, or role-linked records. If the flow is observable or insufficiently protected, individuals can be identified from the transmitted data.
assumptions: The flow includes direct identifiers or combinations of quasi-identifiers sufficient to single out individuals.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether direct identifiers are present versus pseudonymous records.

title: Over-processing or overexposure of grade data when building multiple audience views
description: P2 reads grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. If P2 uses the same underlying dataset for all audiences without strict audience-specific filtering, it may expose unnecessary details to a given viewer, such as teacher-only comments, other students' information, or more history than needed.
assumptions: P2 constructs multiple role-based views from shared grade datasets and filtering/segregation may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: High-confidence threat concept; tree node is approximate.

title: Secondary use of grade records beyond the original educational viewing purpose
description: Once P2 receives grade records, it may reuse them for analytics, profiling, ranking, behavior monitoring, or other purposes beyond generating the intended student, parent, and teacher views, without the data subjects reasonably expecting such use.
assumptions: P2 has access to retained grade data and there are no strict purpose-limitation controls.
uncertainty_note: Applies where the service performs or enables additional uses beyond view generation; not explicit in the flow description.

title: Insufficient transparency or legal basis for sharing grade records with the grading service
description: The transfer and use of grade records by P2 to generate different audience views may lack adequate notice, role-specific access justification, or another valid legal basis/policy basis, especially for parent access or teacher/student cross-context visibility.
assumptions: Compliance obligations require transparency, purpose limitation, and role-appropriate authorization for educational records processing.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible compliance threat for educational records, but the applicable jurisdictional basis is not specified.
